rows.grounds: compound of aṣṭāṃśa (eighth part), hīna (lacking), and agra (tip); final member in possessive relation

items.question: What width and shape are prescribed for the goddess’s trident tip?
premises: The tip is taken as the measure of reference.
The width is reduced by one eighth of that tip.
The resulting form is described as well-rounded.
items.inference: The goddess’s trident tip must be well-rounded and wide by a measure one eighth less than the tip.
uncertainties: The exact referent of agrasya as the base measure in this ritual context is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: For the goddess, it should be well-rounded and wide, measuring one eighth less than the tip.
